advances: Every coordinate-support block of an arbitrary coordinatewise nonincreasing ternary table has a curvature-cutoff certificate at its prescribed binary corner, with an absolute loss. A largest block therefore supplies the required scale after division by the number of blocks. The proof consolidates the distinct Boolean disjoint-pair inequalities underlying the supplied arguments, including the stronger self-family exponent. For actual fiber volumes, the accepted curvature consumer turns the certificate into a mixed-integer depth bound at a point in that same corner fiber. The scalar assertion does not require nonnegative curvature. No reduction from unrestricted convex-body profiles to monotone ternary profiles is asserted.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. The Boolean and scalar assertions are proved in full above. The only accepted input is the actual-body even-thinning depth conclusion and actual-fiber curvature nonnegativity from the declared predecessor. The three supplied external transcripts were read as unverified source material; none of their assertions or reported computations is used as a premise.
proof:
First prove the Boolean assertions. Empty families have both sides zero whenever they occur in a pair count, and their weighted sizes are zero, so they can be set aside. Fix \(0<\theta\le1\) and put \(\beta:=\log_2(1+\theta)\in(0,1]\). We prove \(\mathfrak m_\theta(\mathcal F)\ge|\mathcal F|^\beta\) by induction on \(|E|\). In dimension zero it is equality for both possible downsets. In higher dimension, split \(\mathcal F\) by one coordinate into downsets \(\mathcal F_0,\mathcal F_1\subseteq2^{E\setminus\{i\}}\), where \(\mathcal F_1\subseteq\mathcal F_0\). Put \(a:=|\mathcal F_0|\) and \(b:=|\mathcal F_1|\), so \(0\le b\le a\). The induction hypothesis gives \(\mathfrak m_\theta(\mathcal F)\ge a^\beta+\theta b^\beta\).

If \(a=0\) then the family is empty; if \(b=0\) the desired inequality is immediate. Otherwise put \(u=b/a\in(0,1]\). The function \(h(u):=((1+u)^\beta-1)/u^\beta\) has derivative \(h'(u)=\beta u^{-\beta-1}(1-(1+u)^{\beta-1})\ge0\). Thus \(h(u)\le h(1)=2^\beta-1=\theta\), which is equivalent to \(a^\beta+\theta b^\beta\ge(a+b)^\beta\). This closes the induction. In particular, \(\mathfrak m_{1/2}(\mathcal F)\ge|\mathcal F|^{\log_2(3/2)}\ge\sqrt{|\mathcal F|}\): the exponent is greater than \(1/2\) because \(9/4>2\), and the family size is a nonnegative integer.

For the overlap-deletion count, give each ordered source pair \((R,Q)\in\mathcal A\times\mathcal B\) weight \(2^{-|Q|}\) and send it to \((R\setminus Q,Q)\). Downward closure of \(\mathcal A\) makes the output an ordered disjoint pair in \(\mathcal A\times\mathcal B\). A fixed output \((P,Q)\) has at most \(2^{|Q|}\) preimages, since any preimage has \(R=P\cup I\) for some \(I\subseteq Q\). Its total incoming weight is therefore at most one. Summing source weights proves \(\mathfrak D(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)\ge|\mathcal A|\mathfrak m_{1/2}(\mathcal B)\). Swapping the two families proves also \(\mathfrak D(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)\ge|\mathcal B|\mathfrak m_{1/2}(\mathcal A)\).

Since \(|\mathcal A|\ge\mathfrak m_{1/2}(\mathcal A)\), the first of these estimates proves the cross-family weighted bound. Applying the square-root lower bounds to both estimates, multiplying them, and taking a square root gives
\[
\mathfrak D(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)^2
\ge \bigl(|\mathcal A|\sqrt{|\mathcal B|}\bigr)
       \bigl(|\mathcal B|\sqrt{|\mathcal A|}\bigr)
=(|\mathcal A|\,|\mathcal B|)^{3/2},
\]
which proves the stated cross-family cardinality bound. For \(\mathcal A=\mathcal B=\mathcal F\), the same deletion argument and the sharper weighted-size estimate give
\[
\mathfrak D(\mathcal F,\mathcal F)
\ge|\mathcal F|\mathfrak m_{1/2}(\mathcal F)
\ge|\mathcal F|^{1+\log_2(3/2)}
=|\mathcal F|^{\log_2 3}.
\]
The comparison with exponent \(3/2\) follows from \(3^2>2^3\), including family sizes zero and one.

To verify also the distinct weighted bound with parameter \(\sqrt3-1\), write \(\theta=\sqrt3-1\), so \(\theta+\theta^2/2=1\). Give \((R,Q)\in\mathcal F^2\) weight \(\theta^{|R|+|Q|}\). Partition \(R\cap Q\) randomly into \(I_A,I_B\), assigning each element to either part independently with probability \(1/2\), and output \(A:=R\setminus I_B\), \(B:=Q\setminus I_A\). The output is disjoint, and both sets remain in \(\mathcal F\) by downward closure.

For a fixed disjoint output \((A,B)\), every possible preimage and assignment is specified by \(I_A\subseteq A\), \(I_B\subseteq B\), \(R=A\cup I_B\), and \(Q=B\cup I_A\), subject to \(R,Q\in\mathcal F\). The probability of that assignment is \(2^{-|I_A|-|I_B|}\). Dropping the membership restrictions bounds the total expected incoming weight by
\[
\begin{aligned}
\theta^{|A|+|B|}
\sum_{I_A\subseteq A}\sum_{I_B\subseteq B}
   (\theta/2)^{|I_A|+|I_B|}
&=\bigl[\theta(1+\theta/2)\bigr]^{|A|+|B|}\\
&=1.
\end{aligned}
\]
Summing over outputs gives \(\mathfrak m_{\sqrt3-1}(\mathcal F)^2\le\mathfrak D(\mathcal F,\mathcal F)\). The weighted-size inequality already proved gives \(\mathfrak m_{\sqrt3-1}(\mathcal F)^2\ge|\mathcal F|^{2\log_2\sqrt3}=|\mathcal F|^{\log_2 3}\). This completes all Boolean assertions without using the supplied transcripts as premises.

Now fix the scalar table. Its finite support makes every displacement set and every sum finite. At any positive center, zero belongs to \(\widetilde{\mathcal U}_j\), has mass \(\widetilde w_j\), and has curvature zero. Curvature and reflected mass are even in \(v\). The maximum defining \(\widetilde K_j\) is attained: for any \(L\ge0\), replace it by the largest element not exceeding \(L\) of the finite set \(\{0\}\cup\{\widetilde\Delta_j(v):v\in\widetilde{\mathcal U}_j,\ \widetilde\Delta_j(v)>0\}\). This preserves the numerator and weakly decreases the denominator. Negative curvature values are included already at zero, so no nonnegativity assumption has been used.

Fix any \(T\) with \(\widetilde W_T>0\), and abbreviate \(j=j_T\). Some \(j+\mathbf1_R\), \(R\subseteq T\), has positive weight, and \(j\le j+\mathbf1_R\) coordinatewise, so \(\widetilde w_j>0\). Define \(b(R):=\widetilde w_{j+\mathbf1_R}/\widetilde w_j\) for \(R\subseteq T\). Then \(b(\varnothing)=1\), \(0\le b(R)\le1\), \(b\) is nonincreasing under inclusion, and \(\sum_{R\subseteq T}b(R)=\widetilde W_T/\widetilde w_j\).

For \(t\ge0\), let \(\mathcal F_t:=\{R\subseteq T:b(R)\ge e^{-t}\}\), and put \(N(t):=|\mathcal F_t|\). It is a nonempty Boolean downset. An ordered disjoint pair \((R,Q)\in\mathcal F_t^2\) gives \(v=\mathbf1_R-\mathbf1_Q\). Both \(j+v\) and \(j-v\) belong to the ternary cube, and
\[
\begin{aligned}
j+v&\le j+\mathbf1_R,
&\widetilde w_{j+v}&\ge \widetilde w_j b(R)\ge\widetilde w_j e^{-t},\\
j-v&\le j+\mathbf1_Q,
&\widetilde w_{j-v}&\ge \widetilde w_j b(Q)\ge\widetilde w_j e^{-t}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently \(v\in\widetilde{\mathcal U}_j\), \(\widetilde\alpha(v)\ge\widetilde w_j e^{-t}\), and \(\widetilde\Delta_j(v)\le2t\). Only this upper curvature bound is needed. The positive and negative coordinate supports of \(v\) recover \(R\) and \(Q\), respectively, so the map is injective. It counts both orientations separately, and \((\varnothing,\varnothing)\) gives the zero displacement once. The Boolean bound therefore proves the stronger threshold estimate
\[
\widetilde B_j^\Delta(2t)
\ge \widetilde w_j e^{-t}\mathfrak D(\mathcal F_t,\mathcal F_t)
\ge \widetilde w_j e^{-t}N(t)^{\log_2 3}
\ge \widetilde w_j e^{-t}N(t)^{3/2}.
\]

Put \(R_T:=\max_{t\ge0}e^{-t}N(t)^{3/2}/(1+2t)\). This maximum is attained among the finite nonempty set of thresholds \(\{-\log b(R):R\subseteq T,\ b(R)>0\}\). Indeed, \(N(t)\) changes only at those thresholds and is constant between consecutive thresholds, whereas \(e^{-t}/(1+2t)\) is decreasing. The same argument applies after the last threshold. Since \(b(\varnothing)=1\), zero is a threshold and \(R_T\ge N(0)^{3/2}\ge1\). The definition gives \(N(t)\le R_T^{2/3}e^{2t/3}(1+2t)^{2/3}\).

For every \(b\in[0,1]\), including \(b=0\), one has \(b=\int_0^\infty e^{-t}\mathbf1_{\{b\ge e^{-t}\}}\,dt\). Sum this finite family of identities and apply the preceding estimate to obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\widetilde W_T}{\widetilde w_j}
&=\int_0^\infty e^{-t}N(t)\,dt\\
&\le R_T^{2/3}
       \int_0^\infty e^{-t/3}(1+2t)^{2/3}\,dt\\
&\le 3\,7^{2/3} R_T^{2/3}
\le 3\,7^{2/3} R_T.
\end{aligned}
\]
For the penultimate inequality, apply Hölder with exponents \(3\) and \(3/2\) to the product \(e^{-t/9}\,[e^{-2t/9}(1+2t)^{2/3}]\). The two integrals after taking powers are \(\int_0^\infty e^{-t/3}\,dt=3\) and \(\int_0^\infty e^{-t/3}(1+2t)\,dt=21\). Their Hölder product is \(3^{1/3}21^{2/3}=3\,7^{2/3}\). The last inequality uses \(R_T\ge1\).

Choose a maximizing threshold \(t_T\). The established threshold estimate gives
\[
\frac{\widetilde B_j^\Delta(2t_T)}{1+2t_T}
\ge \widetilde w_j R_T
\ge \frac{\widetilde W_T}{3\,7^{2/3}}.
\]
Its cutoff belongs to the finite set specified in the statement. The strict comparison with \(\widetilde W_T/11\) follows from \((3\,7^{2/3})^3=1323<1331=11^3\). Nothing in this argument required \(T\) to maximize its block mass. It also covers \(T=\varnothing\), for which the block and the threshold family each consist of one element and \(t_T=0\).

Every ternary point has the unique representation \(z=j_T+\mathbf1_R\), with \(T=\{i:z_i>0\}\) and \(R=\{i:z_i=2\}\subseteq T\). Thus the blocks partition the cube, and \(\sum_T\widetilde W_T=\widetilde W\). A largest block has \(\widetilde W_T\ge2^{-n}\widetilde W>0\), proving the global scalar assertion while preserving the center already fixed by that block.

For the actual-body consequence, apply the scalar result with \(\widetilde w_z=w_z\), hence \(\widetilde W=W\) and \(\widetilde W_T=W_T\). At each positive center use precisely the notation of accepted fact 280b299bc1e87c14: \(\alpha(v)=\min\{w_{j+v},w_{j-v}\}\), \(\mathcal U_j=\{v:\alpha(v)>0\}\), \(\Delta_j(v)=\log(w_j^2/(w_{j+v}w_{j-v}))\) on \(\mathcal U_j\), and \(B_j^\Delta(L)=\sum_{v\in\mathcal U_j:\Delta_j(v)\le L}\alpha(v)\). Thus \(\widetilde\alpha(v)=\alpha(v)\), \(\widetilde{\mathcal U}_j=\mathcal U_j\), \(\widetilde\Delta_j(v)=\Delta_j(v)\), and \(\widetilde B_j^\Delta(L)=B_j^\Delta(L)\). Actual-body curvature is nonnegative by that accepted fact. The preceding scalar example is outside these actual-body hypotheses.

Fix \(T\) with \(W_T>0\), choose \(j=j_T\), and choose the finite cutoff \(L=2t_T\ge0\) just proved. In the even-thinning clause of 280b299bc1e87c14 take \(q_v:=\alpha(v)\) for \(v\in\mathcal U_j\) with \(\Delta_j(v)\le L\), and \(q_v:=0\) otherwise. This is exactly that predecessor's thinning variable \(q_v\), with \(0\le q_v\le\alpha(v)\). Its mass \(M_q=\sum_vq_v=B_j^\Delta(L)\) is positive because \(q_0=w_j>0\), and its mean curvature satisfies \(0\le\overline\Delta_{j,q}\le L\). All the predecessor's hypotheses hold: \(n,d\ge1\), \(C\) is a convex body, \(W>0\), and the chosen integer fiber has positive volume. Its fixed-center clause gives one \(x_T^\star\in C_j\), selected before every halfspace, with
\[
\begin{aligned}
h_S((j,x_T^\star))
&\ge \frac{\ell M_q}{16(\overline\Delta_{j,q}+\log2)}
\ge \frac{\ell}{16}\frac{B_j^\Delta(L)}{1+L}\\
&\ge \frac{\ell}{48\,7^{2/3}}W_T.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(\log2<1\). This use of the thinning clause, rather than only a maximum over centers, proves the claimed location of the point in the prescribed corner fiber. Selecting a largest block now gives the stated \(2^{-n}W\) bound at a single point. The definition of \(h_S\) then gives the same lower bound for every closed ambient halfspace containing that point. Since \(e>2\), \(0<\ell<1\), and since \(e<3\), the constant satisfies \(0<\ell/(48\,7^{2/3})<1/e\).

Finally, suppose the table has the indicated form after an integer affine base change. Define \(\widehat C:=\{(z,x):(z_0+Uz,x)\in C\}\), which is a convex body because the change is invertible affine. Its fiber at \(z\) is \(C_{z_0+Uz}\), and \(z\mapsto z_0+Uz\) bijects \(\mathbb Z^n\). Thus the total mixed volume and all corresponding block masses are unchanged. At corresponding centers and displacements the exact maps are \(j\mapsto z_0+Uj\), \(v\mapsto Uv\); these preserve the endpoint minimum, curvature, and oriented cutoff sums, including zero. The ambient affine map bijects closed halfspaces and acts identically on each continuous fiber, so it preserves mixed halfspace masses and point depths. Apply the proved result to \(\widehat C\) and map its point back. Its original base is \(z_0+Uj_T\), as asserted.
statement:
Let \(n\ge1\) be an integer. Let \(\widetilde w:\{0,1,2\}^n\to[0,\infty)\) satisfy \(\widetilde w_y\ge\widetilde w_z\) whenever \(y\le z\) coordinatewise within the ternary cube. Extend it by zero to the rest of \(\mathbb Z^n\), and assume \(\widetilde W:=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}\widetilde w_z>0\).

For each \(j\in\mathbb Z^n\) with \(\widetilde w_j>0\), define \(\widetilde\alpha(v):=\min\{\widetilde w_{j+v},\widetilde w_{j-v}\}\) for \(v\in\mathbb Z^n\), and \(\widetilde{\mathcal U}_j:=\{v:\widetilde\alpha(v)>0\}\). Define \(\widetilde\Delta_j(v):=\log(\widetilde w_j^2/(\widetilde w_{j+v}\widetilde w_{j-v}))\) only on \(\widetilde{\mathcal U}_j\). For \(L\ge0\), put \(\widetilde B_j^\Delta(L):=\sum_{v\in\widetilde{\mathcal U}_j:\,\widetilde\Delta_j(v)\le L}\widetilde\alpha(v)\) and \(\widetilde K_j:=\max_{L\ge0}\widetilde B_j^\Delta(L)/(1+L)\). Every displacement sum is oriented and includes zero. All logarithms other than the explicitly written \(\log_2\) are natural.

These are scalar extensions of the definitions in accepted fact 280b299bc1e87c14: at a fixed center, its \(\alpha(v),\mathcal U_j,\Delta_j(v),B_j^\Delta(L)\) correspond respectively to \(\widetilde\alpha(v),\widetilde{\mathcal U}_j,\widetilde\Delta_j(v),\widetilde B_j^\Delta(L)\). In this scalar extension \(\widetilde\Delta_j\) can be negative, and the cutoff includes such terms. For example, in dimension one the monotone weights \((\widetilde w_0,\widetilde w_1,\widetilde w_2)=(4,1,1)\) have \(\widetilde\Delta_1(1)=-\log4\). No geometric conclusion is drawn from a scalar table unless it satisfies the actual-body hypotheses below.

For \(T\subseteq[n]:=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), let \(j_T:=\mathbf1_T\), where \(\mathbf1_T\) is its indicator vector, and let
\[
\widetilde W_T
:=\sum_{\substack{z\in\{0,1,2\}^n\\\{i:z_i>0\}=T}}\widetilde w_z
=\sum_{R\subseteq T}\widetilde w_{j_T+\mathbf1_R}.
\]
For every \(T\) with \(\widetilde W_T>0\), the center \(j_T\) has positive weight and satisfies
\[
\widetilde K_{j_T}
\ge \frac{\widetilde W_T}{3\,7^{2/3}}
> \frac{\widetilde W_T}{11}.
\]
The center is prescribed by \(T\), before every threshold and cutoff. A cutoff attaining the stated lower bound can be selected from the finite set
\[
\left\{
2\log\frac{\widetilde w_{j_T}}{\widetilde w_{j_T+\mathbf1_R}}:
R\subseteq T,\ \widetilde w_{j_T+\mathbf1_R}>0
\right\}.
\]
Consequently a largest-mass block supplies a binary center \(j_T\) for which \(\widetilde K_{j_T}\ge(3\,7^{2/3})^{-1}2^{-n}\widetilde W\).

The Boolean inequalities used here have the following independent scope. For a finite ground set \(E\), a downset is a family closed under taking subsets; the empty family is permitted. For downsets \(\mathcal A,\mathcal B\subseteq2^E\), define the ordered disjoint-pair count \(\mathfrak D(\mathcal A,\mathcal B):=|\{(R,Q)\in\mathcal A\times\mathcal B:R\cap Q=\varnothing\}|\). For a downset \(\mathcal F\subseteq2^E\) and \(0<\theta\le1\), define \(\mathfrak m_\theta(\mathcal F):=\sum_{R\in\mathcal F}\theta^{|R|}\). Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathfrak m_\theta(\mathcal F)
&\ge |\mathcal F|^{\log_2(1+\theta)},\\
\mathfrak D(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)
&\ge (|\mathcal A|\,|\mathcal B|)^{3/4},\\
\mathfrak D(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)
&\ge \mathfrak m_{1/2}(\mathcal A)\mathfrak m_{1/2}(\mathcal B),\\
\mathfrak D(\mathcal F,\mathcal F)
&\ge |\mathcal F|\,\mathfrak m_{1/2}(\mathcal F)
 \ge |\mathcal F|^{\log_2 3}
 \ge |\mathcal F|^{3/2},\\
\mathfrak D(\mathcal F,\mathcal F)
&\ge \mathfrak m_{\sqrt3-1}(\mathcal F)^2
 \ge |\mathcal F|^{\log_2 3}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The inequalities hold also for empty families, using \(0^a=0\) for \(a>0\). Empty sets are allowed in every ordered pair.

For the actual-body consequence, let \(n,d\ge1\) be integers, let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body, and define \(C_z:=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}\) for \(z\in\mathbb R^n\), \(w_z:=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z)\), with zero volume for empty or lower-dimensional fibers, \(W:=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}w_z>0\), and \(S:=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\). Define \(h_S(p):=\inf_{H\ni p}\mathcal H_d(S\cap H)\), over closed ambient halfspaces. These are exactly the actual-body objects in accepted fact 280b299bc1e87c14. Suppose \(w_z=0\) for every integer \(z\notin\{0,1,2\}^n\), and \(w_y\ge w_z\) whenever \(y,z\in\{0,1,2\}^n\) and \(y\le z\) coordinatewise.

Set \(W_T:=\sum_{R\subseteq T}w_{j_T+\mathbf1_R}\) and \(\ell:=-\log(1-e^{-1})\). For every \(T\) with \(W_T>0\), there is one \(x_T^\star\in C_{j_T}\) such that
\[
h_S((j_T,x_T^\star))
\ge \frac{\ell}{48\,7^{2/3}}W_T.
\]
In particular, there is one \(p^\star\in S\) such that every closed ambient halfspace \(H\) containing it satisfies
\[
\mathcal H_d(S\cap H)
\ge \frac{\ell}{48\,7^{2/3}}\,2^{-n}W
> \frac{\ell}{176}\,2^{-n}W.
\]
The constant \(\ell/(48\,7^{2/3})\) is absolute and belongs to \((0,1/e)\). There are no additional restrictions on the fiber shapes or on \(d\).

The actual-body conclusions also hold after an integer affine change of the base: it suffices that \(z\mapsto w_{z_0+Uz}\) obey the stated ternary support and monotonicity conditions for some \(z_0\in\mathbb Z^n\) and \(U\in\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb Z)\). The point associated with block \(T\) then lies in the original fiber with base \(z_0+Uj_T\).
